definitions: A class of models used in machine learning, primarily for classification or regression tasks, that learn a direct mapping from input features to output labels.
Models that focus on distinguishing between different classes or categories by learning the decision boundary between them, rather than modeling the underlying distribution of the data.
examples: Logistic regression is a common example of discriminative models.
Unlike generative models, discriminative models do not model the joint probability distribution.
The performance of discriminative models often depends on the quality of feature engineering.
